review: The hymn is the presence of Christ in trouble: 1:1–4 is Matt 28:20 (אֲנִי אִתְּכֶם) with Rom 8:28, 2:1–4 is 2 Cor 4:17 (כְּבוֹד לֹא נֶעֱרָךְ) nearly verbatim, 3:1–4 is Phil 4:4 with 1 Thess 4:16, and 4:1–4 is 1 John 3:2 with 1 Thess 4:14.

2:3 uses נֶעֱרָךְ, the Niphal of עָרַךְ, to say the pain is 'not to be compared' with the glory; this is the verb of Isa 40:18 and Ps 89:7 for placing one thing beside another, so the line is a comparison denied rather than a quantity measured.
3:3 keeps the second person (תָּבוֹא אֵלֵינוּ) in a stanza that otherwise speaks about Him, because the Arabic سَتَجِيءُ is addressed to Him and the turn is the point.
